literature_notes: All five ledger clips were examined. L1, L2, L4, and L5 all describe full-length ANTXR2 (CMG2 isoform 4) carrying a C-terminal V5 tag, cloned into pcDNA3.1/V5-HIS-TOPO or pcDNA3.5/V5-HIS-TOPO vectors (which append V5-His to the C-terminus of the insert). The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 340–489) firmly in the intracellular compartment; the V5 tag therefore faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space. These constructs are recorded in other_positions as intracellular tags. L3 describes an HA-tagged construct of ANTXR1 (TEM8/isoform 1), a paralog — not ANTXR2 — and no residue position is stated; it cannot ground any ANTXR2 site. No ledger clip reports a tag, fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon insertion, or any other tolerated insertion on the extracellular face of ANTXR2. The large extracellular domain (residues 34–318) and the mature N-terminus (residue 34, after signal-peptide cleavage at 33) are both unaddressed by the ledger. Zero extracellular sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal V5 tag on full-length CMG2/4 (ANTXR2 isoform 4) confirmed by Western blot; the C-terminus (residues 340–489) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
CMG2-V5 (C-terminal V5, intracellular) expressed in HeLa cells and used in [³H]-palmitate S-acylation assay; tag is on the cytoplasmic tail and is not a surface epitope.
